evidence:
Scope: the three scored dimensions are batched weighted_mean (functional/judge.toml:3,21 with 152 criteria; polish/judge.toml:3,15 with 5; visual/judge.toml:3,15 with 5). Both gates are aggregation = "all_pass" (gates/render/judge.toml:15, gates/constraints/judge.toml:15), one criterion each, and are exempt. Frozen prompt/judge hashes I computed match manifest.json lines 36-42.

Functional (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:15): "Once this basic gate succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure, and preserve successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared scenarios reduce repeated setup; they are not conjunctive scoring bundles." Same line: "Preserve every other completed row and never infer its failure from the missing evidence." Line 9: "give that criterion its lowest score (binary 0; Likert 1), state what you observed, and move on." Reinforced per protocol: line 23 "a failed cell must not erase successful sibling cells"; line 55 "do not make later concurrency credit inherit the earlier pair's failure"; lines 61/63/73 "If one branch fails, establish a simpler eligible setup for independent observations. The failed branch's own criterion stays 0."

Polish (tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:12): "Otherwise judge each criterion independently, continue after failures and preserve valid observations. A failed recovery branch must not erase other observed recovery credit." Line 14: "Continue independent checks after any sibling failure." Line 7 carries the same "move on" sentence.

Visual (tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:12): "Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures." Line 16: "Preserve every completed independent observation."

The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the in-dimension global browser gate (functional:15, polish:12, visual:12), which the template also has ("The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension", template polish prompt.md:19-20) and which check 29 requires; it is not a stop-on-first-criterion-failure rule. The task wording is at least as strong as the template's ("Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion", template functional prompt.md:68-69).

Stop-wording search: a regex scan of the three scored prompts and all 162 scored criterion descriptions for stop at/on/after, first fail, do not continue, skip remaining/rest, abort, fail all/every, remaining criteria, zero the/all, and 'if/requires/only if/unless hro_<id>' found zero hits. The 14 criteria that name another criterion id (e.g. functional/judge.toml:438 hro_commitment -> hro_history, :1329 hro_live_stale_mark -> hro_change_aba, polish/judge.toml:36 hro_pol_focus -> hro_pol_change_recovery) use it only to delimit ownership ("belongs to hro_...") or to reuse a setup, never to inherit a verdict; functional/judge.toml:672 states "do not require the earlier concurrent stage to pass".

Adversarial reads. Broken app that could pass: none arises from this row, since independence wording only stops one miss removing other credit; a blank/static shell is still zeroed by the in-dimension gate. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app with one broken transition (e.g. P4 revision) is not cascaded, because the prompt orders fresh equivalent setup for other rows (functional:15, 61, 63, 73). One residual coupling, not a row-38 wording defect: functional/judge.toml:1320 hro_desk_field_refusal says "If no malformed term is ever refused there is no explanation to observe: give0", so it shares a product precondition with hro_change_numeric. That is the positive-control rule for a row owning the refusal's explanation, and belongs to rows 28/40 if anyone objects.

Limits of this evidence: check-batched-independence-wording.py is a private checker and was NOT executed; its documented behaviour (deterministic-checks.md:54) was applied by hand. No full configured judge run exists in raw-evidence-index.json (its scope says full configured grading is absent), so whether the configured judge actually returns independent verdicts for all 152 functional criteria after a failure is unmeasured; that is workload/runtime evidence owned by other rows and is not required by this wording check, so risk is false here.
